knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Grease stops paint from bonding. The surface is washed, rinsed and dried before painting, and the step is recorded.
High-pressure water can strip sound paint, roughen timber, damage render and drive water behind a surface. The lesson gives no pressure figure, so none is assumed.
A powder on the finger suggests chalking. It is brushed or washed off, and the surface is checked, before any coat goes on.
Damp and dryness are checked before the first coat. Paint over damp or residue is a common cause of failure.

practicalCriteria: On a sample greasy wall, the worker records the inspection findings (grease, chalking, efflorescence, mould, loose paint, damp) with the location of each, before any cleaning starts.
The worker selects a cleaner and method suited to the simulated contamination, gives the product name and its data sheet reference, and states why the method was chosen.
The worker washes from the bottom up, rinses to remove residue, dries the surface, and records the drying check and the result of the moisture check where the site provides a meter.
On a simulated mould or unknown-contamination patch, the worker stops, records the finding, and refers it without painting the patch.
passRule: Pass when all four practical criteria are observed and recorded by the assessor on a sample surface (a sample board or a designated wall), with no stop-work criterion met. A knowledge check result alone is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Surface preparation record with inspection findings, method, product, rinse and drying check
Photographs of the sample surface before and after preparation, taken with permission
Referral record for the simulated mould or unknown patch
stopWorkCriteria: Painting begins over damp, mould or unknown contamination
High-pressure water is used on old paint, render, timber or near electrical fittings
Two cleaning products are mixed without checking the data sheets
